subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw core support beyond the shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK and command-cron paths, and what owner/security gates are required?
rationale: The remaining scope can expose filesystem, process, session, Gateway, cron, and node actions without a model turn, so automation cannot safely choose the supported product boundary or security model.

options.title: Keep narrow gated slices
options.body: Leave this umbrella open while reviewing the active host-filesystem and readiness PRs, requiring explicit owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Stop at shipped paths
options.body: Declare HTTP/RPC/SDK and command-cron support sufficient, then reject or close host-FS, exec, slash, and generic CLI direct dispatch until a new maintainer-sponsored proposal exists.

options.title: Approve broader direct execution
options.body: Allow broader direct tool execution only after maintainers approve a named security design, upgrade proof, and operator-facing controls that make the risk explicit.

recommendation.title: Keep narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Leave this umbrella open while reviewing the active host-filesystem and readiness PRs, requiring explicit owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily the dangerous-tool and owner-gated Gateway security boundary, and recent history ties steipete to that boundary.
